question.text:
A $3$2-bit system uses $\mathbf{4}$ KB pages and a two-level page table with a $10$-bit Level-$1$ index, $10$-bit Level-$2$ index, and $12$-bit page offset.

The current Level-$1$ page table begins at physical address $\texttt{0x2000}$.

Relevant entries are:

$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline
\textbf{Page-table location} & \textbf{Entry} \\ \hline
\text{L1[0]} & \texttt{0x1007} \\
\text{L1[3]} & \texttt{0x3007} \\
\text{table at }\texttt{0x1000},\ \text{entry }0 & \texttt{0x7007} \\
\text{table at }\texttt{0x1000},\ \text{entry }1 & \texttt{0x8007} \\
\text{table at }\texttt{0x3000},\ \text{entry }128 & \texttt{0xA007} \\
\hline
\end{array}
$$

All unspecified entries are zero and therefore not present. The low permission bits are removed when obtaining the physical page address.

Which translations are correct?

  1. $\texttt{0x00000FFF} \rightarrow \texttt{0x00007FFF}$
     
  2. $\texttt{0x00001000} \rightarrow \texttt{0x00008000}$
     
  3. $\texttt{0x00C08003} \rightarrow \texttt{0x0000A003}$
     
  4. $\texttt{0x00C80003} \rightarrow \texttt{0x0000A003}$

question.text:
A system uses:

  • $4$ KB pages
     
  • A $4$-entry fully associative TLB
     
  • LRU replacement
     

$$ \textbf{Initial TLB:} $$$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Valid} & \text{VPN} & \text{Physical Page} & \text{LRU} \\
\hline
1 & 11 & 12 & 2 \\
1 & 7 & 4 & 3 \\
1 & 3 & 6 & 4 \\
0 & 4 & 9 & 1 \\
\hline
\end{array}
$$

$$ \textbf{Relevant initial page-table entries:} $$ $$
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{VPN} & \text{Valid} & \text{Location} \\
\hline
0 & 1 & \text{Physical page }5 \\
1 & 0 & \text{Disk} \\
2 & 0 & \text{Disk} \\
3 & 1 & \text{Physical page }6 \\
7 & 1 & \text{Physical page }4 \\
11 & 1 & \text{Physical page }12 \\
\hline
\end{array}
$$

When a page fault occurs, new physical pages are allocated beginning with physical page $13$.

The following virtual addresses are accessed in order:

$\texttt{0x0FFF}$
$\texttt{0x7A28}$
$\texttt{0x3DAD}$
$\texttt{0x3A98}$
$\texttt{0x1C19}$
$\texttt{0x1000}$
$\texttt{0x22D0}$

Which statements are correct?

  1. The access to $\texttt{0x0FFF}$ produces a TLB miss but not a page fault.
     
  2. The accesses to $\texttt{0x7A28}, \texttt{0x3DAD}, \texttt{0x3A98},$ and $\texttt{0x1000}$ are all TLB hits.
     
  3. Accessing $\texttt{0x1C19}$ causes a page fault, after which VPN $1$ is mapped to physical page $13$.
     
  4. After all seven accesses have completed, VPN $0$ is still present in the TLB.

question.text:
A machine uses a two-level page table. The page-directory base address is held in a register.

Assume:

  • One physical-memory access takes $100$ ns
     
  • Page directories and page tables are always resident in memory
     
  • $0.001%$ of user-memory accesses cause a page fault
     
  • Servicing a page fault takes $10$ ms
     
  • Initially there is no cache
     
  • A TLB is added such that $75\%$ of translations are found in the TLB
     
  • TLB lookup time may be ignored
     
  • A translation found in the TLB corresponds to a resident page
     

What is the effective memory access time, in nanoseconds?

question.text:
A machine has:

  • $64$-bit virtual addresses
     
  • $8$ KB pages
     
  • $4$ GB physical memory
     
  • $512$ TLB entries
     
  • An inverted page table with one entry per physical frame
     
  • Each inverted page-table entry occupies $8$ bytes
     

Which statements are correct?

  1. The virtual page number requires $51$ bits.
     
  2. If all $512$ TLB entries contain distinct valid translations, the TLB reach is $4$ MB.
     
  3. The TLB can simultaneously cover $\frac{1}{512}$ of physical memory.
     
  4. The inverted page table occupies $4$ MB.

question.text:
A virtual-memory system has:

  • $48$-bit virtual addresses
     
  • $32$ KB pages
     
  • $32$ TB physical memory
     
  • Two-level page tables
     
  • Both levels stored in physical memory
     
  • Every second-level page table must fit completely inside one page frame
     
  • Page-table entries are stored using the minimum whole number of bytes sufficient to contain the physical page number
     

Which of the following correctly gives the bit division

$$(\text{Level-1 index},\text{ Level-2 index},\text{ page offset})?$$

  1. $(20,13,15)$
     
  2. $(18,15,15)$
     
  3. $(21,12,15)$
     
  4. $(13,20,15)$
